standard-dialogue.npc: Hello mortal. Have you come to retrieve something you lost when you died?

options.text: How does that work?

steps.player: How does that work?

steps.npc: When you die, you often drop things you were carrying. In most cases, a gravestone appears near where you died, and your items can be retrieved there.
However, gravestones do not last for long. When your gravestone collapses, your items come here, to me. I can return them to you - though I charge a fee for my services.
Aside from that, if you bring me your unwanted possessions, and sacrifice them into my Coffer here, I'll count their value against any future fees I charge you.
I don't accept just any junk, but I'll try to give you a good price for anything decent.
So do you need to retrieve something you lost when you died?

options.text: What is this place?

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: As you should be able to see, I am Death. The Grim Reaper. The Inexorable One. The Inescapable Grasp of Mortal Destiny. And this is my little office. Nice, isn't it?

options.text: It's lovely.

steps.player: It's lovely.

steps.npc: Thank you. I feel the colour scheme suits my style. Now, can I help you retrieve something you lost when you died?

options.text: Your decorations leave a bit to be desired.

steps.player: Your decorations leave a bit to be desired.

steps.npc: Sometimes it's hard to care for beauty when one's very existence is just seen as a curse upon the world. Now, do you actually want to retrieve something from me?

options.text: Yes, have you got anything for me?

steps.player: Yes, have you got anything for me?

steps.text: Death's Office Item Retrieval interface opens.

options.text: More options...
Can I choose a different-looking gravestone?

steps.player: Can I choose a different-looking gravestone?

steps.text: The player is then given a choice between the basic or angel gravestone, which are free and 200k coins respectively.
If the player chooses the angel gravestone without 200,000 coins:

steps.npc: You haven't got 200,000 coins to pay for that. I can take coins from your inventory, or from my Coffer.

options.text: Can I choose a different-looking gravestone?

steps.player: Can I choose a different-looking gravestone?

options.text: Actually, never mind.

steps.player: Actually, never mind.

steps.text: If the player chooses the angel gravestone with 200,000 coins:

steps.npc: Most people won't see your grave, by the way. It appears to you, but it aims to be invisible to everyone else. Are you sure you want to buy a cosmetic override for it?

options.text: Yes, I understand other people won't often see it.

steps.player: Yes, I understand other people won't often see it.

steps.text: Your gravestone is now the Angel of Death.

steps.npc: It is not for me to judge how people spend their money.

options.text: No thanks, it's not worth it.

steps.player: No thanks, it's not worth it.

steps.npc: It is not for me to judge how people spend their money.

steps.text: If the player chooses the basic gravestone while already having the angel gravestone:

steps.npc: Do you really want to switch to the basic gravestone? I'm not offering to give back the fee you paid earlier.

options.text: Yes, I want the basic gravestone.

steps.player: Yes, I want the basic gravestone.

steps.text: Your gravestone is now the basic type.

options.text: Actually, never mind.

steps.player: Actually, never mind.

steps.text: If the player chooses the basic gravestone while already having the basic gravestone:

steps.npc: You've already got the basic gravestone.

options.text: Can I choose a different-looking gravestone?

steps.player: Can I choose a different-looking gravestone?

options.text: Actually, never mind.

steps.player: Actually, never mind.

options.text: Can I change how I die?

steps.npc: Er... I suppose so.
How would you like to... die?

steps.text: Death Animations interface opens.

options.text: Not just now, thanks.

steps.player: Not just now, thanks.

steps.npc: Really? There isn't much else for you to do here. But you know your business.

options.text: Previous options...

upon-losing-any-items-while-dying-for-th.npc: So, mortal... you have died, as all mortals do. As you have suffered the loss of some items on this occasion, I have brought you here to explain for you how that works.

upon-losing-any-items-while-dying-for-th.player: I lost items? Can I get them back?

upon-losing-any-items-while-dying-for-th.npc: Let me explain... Across most of the land of Gielinor, when you die, some of the items you're carrying are dropped.

upon-losing-any-items-while-dying-for-th.text: A gravestone appears on the ground near where you died. You can go there and retrieve your items by clicking on it.
Your gravestone would be marked with an arrow to help to spot it. A grave icon appears on the world map too, if your grave is in a mapped area.
Gravestones charge a small fee to return especially valuable items, but most things are returned free of charge. Conveniently, a gravestone can take its fee straight from your bank.
A gravestone does not last forever. After about 15 minutes, a gravestone will collapse. Anything in it will be sent here, to me.

upon-losing-any-items-while-dying-for-th.npc: I will look after such items, without a time limit. However, I do charge more for my services. It would be cheaper to retrieve them from the gravestone directly, if you can reach it in time.

options.text: Tell me about gravestones again.

steps.player: Tell me about gravestones again.

steps.npc: Gladly... Across most of the land of Gielinor, when you die, some of the items you're carrying are dropped.

options.text: How do I pay a gravestone fee?
options.condition: If the player has not gone through with this dialogue option:

steps.player: How do I pay a gravestone fee?

steps.npc: Cash is always acceptable. Also, a gravestone can take it directly from you bank, in case you didn't have enough with you.
Besides that, take a look at my Coffer here. You can bring your unwanted possessions, and sacrifice them into my Coffer. I'll count their value against any future gravestone fees you're charged.

steps.text: Death's Coffer won't accept items worth less than 10,000 coins per item - Death doesn't want cheap junk! But more valuable items can be sacrificed to pay down future reclamation fees.

steps.player: How long do I have to return to my gravestone?

steps.text: A gravestone lasts for at least 15 minutes before it collapses. However, that timer pauses if you become inactive, in case you have lost your connection to the world.
A timer on your head-up display shows the remaining time before your gravestone will collapse.

steps.npc: There is a menu to predict these things for you. Take a look at your Worn Items side-panel...

steps.text: The worn equipment tab opens.
The Items Kept on Death menu tells you roughly what your items will do when you next die, including estimating gravestone fees.
